8.description: The committee received an update on its 2025 work plan, which includes improving accessibility for transit and civic safety.

chips.text: Many in the deafblind community feel CNIB does not provide proper support.
Deafblind Services is a key focus area for the 2025 work plan.
Staff will provide an update on transit hub designs to the committee.

11.description: The education and awareness subcommittee met to discuss accessibility in Saskatoon's established neighborhoods and drafted a letter to a standing policy committee.

chips.text: Whether the deaf and blind subcommittee met was not known.

14.description: The subcommittee's letter identifies multiple accessibility barriers at construction sites, including blocked curb cuts, inaccessible signage, and hazardous detours. This aims to improve safety and navigation for residents with mobility, hearing, or vision impairments.

chips.text: Councillor Dudley suggested residents call the 24-hour customer service line for specific issues.
Residents with mobility, hearing, or vision impairments are affected by construction barriers.
A delegate raised concerns about private e-scooters on sidewalks, speed, and lack of noise.
City staff confirmed a bylaw to legalize private e-scooters will come forward in fall.

15.description: Saskatoon will develop a citywide policy for pedestrian signal volume standards. Councillor Dubois and Director Magus will address immediate issues and report back on solutions.

chips.text: How to regularly monitor pedestrian signal volumes remains unclear.
Low signal volumes create safety risks for deafblind pedestrians.
Director Magus committed to creating a citywide policy on signal volumes.
